2021_219_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.paragraph: Troy School District's Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, prepared by the district's Business Services Department and audited by Plante & Moran, which issued an unmodified opinion dated October 5, 2021. The district served 12,723 students in 20 schools and closed the year with a governmental-activities net position deficit of $(201,057,958), reflecting a net pension liability of $308,094,061 and a net OPEB liability of $48,088,931 under MPSERS. The most consequential operating result was in the General Fund, where fund balance increased $6.7 million to $32,734,102, a sixth consecutive year of growth, leaving the available (unassigned) balance at 19.88 percent of 2021 general operating expenditures.

**Report and opinion**
Annual Comprehensive Financial Report of Troy School District for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021, submitted October 5, 2021 by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, from 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777. Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education, issued an unmodified opinion dated October 5, 2021. There were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards for the year ended June 30, 2021. ASBO International awarded the district a Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989-2019, and the certificate reproduced in the report covers the year ended June 30, 2020.

**Statement of activities**
Total expenses were $203,874,829: instruction $120,915,752, support services $67,702,339, community services $6,324,376, interest $4,533,849, food services $2,416,697, athletics $1,700,708, and other debt costs $281,108. Charges for services totaled $1,802,535 and operating grants and contributions $52,855,894, leaving net expense of $(149,216,400). General revenue of $144,318,096 included property taxes of $39,308,501 for general purposes, $17,345,162 for debt service, and $4,152,751 for capital projects, plus $81,687,900 of unrestricted state aid. Change in net position was $(4,898,304).

**Fund results**
Governmental funds ended with a combined fund balance of $57,844,378, a decrease of $6.2 million. General Fund revenue was $171,189,282 against expenditures of $164,655,892; net change in fund balance was $6,724,392, ending at $32,734,102 (unassigned $31,807,875). The 2019 Capital Projects Fund spent $8,487,133 in capital outlay and ended at $18,231,222. Nonmajor funds ended at $6,879,054. Special revenue fund balance rose from $2.8 million to $3.1 million; debt service funds fell $1.2 million; capital project funds fell $12.1 million. Sinking fund millage collections were $4.1 million.

**Budget**
The final General Fund budget was amended in June 2021, raising budgeted revenue $21.7 million. The original budget assumed a $700 per pupil foundation reduction; state revenue was increased $14.8 million to reflect a flat foundation allowance of $9,315 per pupil plus a one-time $65 per pupil increase, and federal revenue rose $6.8 million (CARES Act CRF of $6.7 million). Actual revenue was $178,422 under final budget; actual expenditures were $1,035,586 under final budget.

**Capital assets and debt**
Capital assets totaled $392,874,746 less accumulated depreciation of $193,697,815, for $199,176,931 net. Additions were $10.8 million; depreciation expense was $9,040,252. Bonds outstanding were $130,280,000 plus $7,678,963 of unamortized premium. The district issued $40,425,000 of refunding bonds and advance refunded $37,860,000 of 2012 and 2014 bonds, reducing debt service over seven years by approximately $4,064,000 for an economic gain of about $2,559,000. Standard & Poor's affirmed the AA/Stable rating in May 2021.

**Pension and OPEB**
Pension contributions were $27,611,786 (including $11,658,202 of state UAAL stabilization funding) and OPEB contributions $6,980,805. Pension expense was $47,852,726; OPEB recovery was $860,940.

**Governance**
Board of Education: Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond, and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Superintendent: Richard Machesky, Ed.D.
2021_219_8_b_24680_troy_school_district_.verbose:
**Identification and issuance.** Annual Comprehensive Financial Report with Supplemental Information of Troy School District, a school district in the State of Michigan, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021. The cover lists the Administration Building at 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone (248) 823-4000, fax (248) 823-4013. The letter of transmittal is dated October 5, 2021 and signed by Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Director of Finance, Business Services, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777 (248.823.4022, rwest@troy.k12.mi.us). Plante & Moran, appointed by the Troy Board of Education, issued an unmodified opinion dated October 5, 2021 plus a Government Auditing Standards report of the same date; there were no findings or questioned costs for federal awards, whose supplemental information was issued under separate cover. ASBO International awarded Certificates of Excellence in Financial Reporting for fiscal years ended June 30, 1989-2019; the certificate reproduced, for the year ended June 30, 2020, is signed by W. Edward Chabal, President, and David J. Lewis, Executive Director.

**Governance and administration.** The seven-member elected Board of Education consisted of Karl Schmidt (President), Dr. Nicole Wilson (Vice President), Gary Hauff (Secretary), and Trustees Vital Anne, Steve Gottlieb, Elizabeth Hammond, and Dr. Nancy Philippart. Administration: Richard Machesky, Ed.D., Superintendent; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services; Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent Secondary Instruction; Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent Employee Services; Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent Elementary Instruction; Kerry Birmingham, Director of Communications and Strategic Initiatives.

**District profile.** Enrollment as of Spring 2021 was 12,723 students in kindergarten through twelfth grade across 20 schools, plus students with developmental disabilities ages 19-26 in the Troy Center for Transition/Grow Program; students speak more than 80 languages at home. The configuration includes 12 elementary schools, four middle schools, two comprehensive high schools, an International Baccalaureate Academy, an alternative high school, and Intersect. The City of Troy covers 26.61 square miles, is the largest city in Oakland County and the 13th largest in Michigan, with a population of 85,584 cited in the transmittal letter, over 6,000 businesses with a market value of over $12 billion, and more than 57 percent of residents holding a bachelor's degree or higher. Eight schools have received the National Blue Ribbon Award (Bemis, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wattles, Larson, Athens, Troy High, and International Academy). Building data include Athens High School (398,426 square feet, built 1974, 1,579 students), Troy High School (343,207 square feet, 1992, 2,100), Baker Middle School (128,458 square feet, 694), Boulan Middle School (111,190 square feet, 1971, 844), Larson Middle School (111,190 square feet, 1971, 733), Smith Middle School (101,094 square feet, 1967, 628), International Academy East (81,455 square feet, 1952, 571), Hamilton Elementary (64,312 square feet, 1983, 458), Hill Elementary (54,456 square feet, 1967, 338), Career High School (37,520 square feet, 1978, 212), the Preschool (72,000 square feet, 2019, 108), and Troy Center for Transitions (2007, 59); totals are 448.74 acres and 2,185,181 square feet.

**Economic condition.** The district received approximately $6.9 million of Coronavirus Relief Funding and ESSER I funds, spent in 2020-2021 on technology, online learning resources, and personal protective equipment, plus ESSER II and ESSER III allocations and a state equity payment of $385 per pupil, with an anticipated further equity payment of more than $900 per pupil in 2021-2022. Standard & Poor's affirmed the AA/Stable rating in May 2021.

**Government-wide statements.** At June 30, 2021 total assets were $283,253,146, including cash and cash equivalents of $24,576,586, other receivables of $367,834, due from other governmental units of $22,481,914, inventory of $126,751, prepaid expenses of $131,932, restricted assets of $36,391,198, capital assets not being depreciated of $3,164,894, and depreciable capital assets net of $196,012,037. Deferred outflows totaled $93,398,741 (deferred charges on bond refunding $517,860; deferred pension costs $69,417,209; deferred OPEB costs $23,463,672). Total liabilities were $528,864,531, including accounts payable $2,509,401, due to other governmental units $5,299,819, accrued salaries and wages $8,951,060, payroll taxes and withholdings $6,403,279, accrued interest payable $606,366, unearned revenue $3,068,278, noncurrent liabilities due within one year $15,588,619 and due in more than one year $130,254,717, net pension liability $308,094,061, and net OPEB liability $48,088,931. Deferred inflows totaled $48,845,314. Net position components were net investment in capital assets $82,174,848, restricted for capital projects $523,276 and food service $281,831, and unrestricted $(284,037,913), for a total deficit of $(201,057,958) against a beginning deficit of $(196,159,654).

**Statement of activities.** Expenses totaled $203,874,829: instruction $120,915,752 (charges $436,849, grants $35,317,057, net $(85,161,846)); support services $67,702,339 (grants $15,135,881, net $(52,566,458)); athletics $1,700,708 (charges $319,969); food services $2,416,697 (charges $35,261, grants $2,402,956, net positive $21,520); community services $6,324,376 (charges $1,010,456); interest $4,533,849; other debt costs $281,108. Program revenue was $1,802,535 in charges and $52,855,894 in operating grants, net expense $(149,216,400). General revenue of $144,318,096 comprised property taxes of $39,308,501 (general), $17,345,162 (debt service), and $4,152,751 (capital projects); unrestricted state aid $81,687,900; unrestricted federal grants $23,088; investment earnings $97,442; loss on disposal of capital assets $(708,156); student activities $1,186,381; and other $1,225,027.

**Governmental funds.** Combined fund balance was $57,844,378 on total assets of $99,844,774 and liabilities of $42,000,396. Fund revenue was $201,492,650 (local $65,117,799; state $110,743,625; federal $15,532,995; interdistrict $10,098,231) and expenditures $206,573,406 (instruction $110,296,670; support services $51,263,342; athletics $1,593,596; food services $2,355,746; community services $3,400,743; principal $12,850,000; interest $5,517,016; other debt costs $281,108; capital outlay $19,015,185), for excess of revenue under expenditures of $(5,080,756). Other financing sources and uses included face value of debt issued $40,425,000, proceeds from sale of capital assets $9,401, transfers in and out of $1,847,391, and payment to a bond refunding escrow agent of $(41,571,042). Net change in fund balances was $(6,217,397) from a beginning balance of $64,061,775. General Fund revenue was $171,189,282 and expenditures $164,655,892, producing $6,533,390 of excess revenue and a $6,724,392 net change; ending fund balance $32,734,102 (unassigned $31,807,875, assigned to subsequent year's budget $706,368, nonspendable inventory $87,927 and prepaids $131,932). The 2019 Capital Projects Fund ended at $18,231,222; nonmajor funds at $6,879,054, including restricted debt service $343,339, capital projects $2,731,074, food service $243,007, committed community service $689,143 and student activities $2,153,131, and assigned capital maintenance $680,536. Custodial funds held cash of $109,854 and accounts payable of $2,057, net position $107,797; additions were $127,342 and deductions $133,591.

**Budgetary comparison, General Fund.** Original budget revenue $149,632,442; final $171,367,704; actual $171,189,282 ($178,422 under final). Original expenditures $161,272,639; final $165,691,478; actual $164,655,892 ($1,035,586 under final). Actual line items included basic programs $87,483,395, added needs $21,334,681, adult/continuing education $759,568, pupil services $11,914,484, instructional staff $10,807,305, general administration $1,171,990, school administration $9,005,170, business $1,665,793, operations and maintenance $11,570,833, pupil transportation $2,833,477, central $2,878,902, athletics $1,616,077, community services $606,808, and debt service $991,754. Budgeted ending fund balance was $15,794,513 original and $31,875,336 final versus $32,734,102 actual. The final amendment, adopted June 2021, raised budgeted revenue $21.7 million, including $14.8 million of state revenue reflecting a flat $9,315 per pupil foundation allowance plus a one-time $65 per pupil increase, $6.8 million of federal revenue (CARES Act CRF of $6.7 million), and $1.0 million of additional PA 18 interdistrict millage funding; $1.4 million of budgeted property sale revenue was removed.

**Capital assets and debt.** Capital assets at cost were $392,874,746 (land $2,086,043; construction in progress $1,078,851; buildings and improvements $339,039,052; furniture and equipment $50,670,800) less accumulated depreciation of $193,697,815. Depreciation expense of $9,040,252 was charged to support services $6,088,627, community services $2,636,613, instruction $265,662, food services $48,017, and athletics $1,333. Construction commitments were $967,251 spent to date with $2,798,369 remaining ($686,281/$1,018,395 sinking fund; $280,970/$1,779,974 other projects). Long-term debt moved from $160,725,023 to $145,843,336, with general obligation bonds of $130,280,000 and premium of $7,678,963; compensated absences ended at $7,666,873 and other termination benefits at $217,500. Outstanding issues include the 2012 $43,580,000 refunding bond (1.89%, $4,160,000 outstanding), 2014 $52,710,000 (4.00-5.00%, $4,000,000), 2015 $31,930,000 refunding (5.00%, $16,200,000), 2016 $40,000,000 (2.94%-4.50%, $32,900,000), 2018 $7,125,000 (3.00%-3.75%, $6,870,000), 2019 $22,630,000 (4.00-5.00%, $19,975,000), 2020 $6,100,000 (2.00%, $5,750,000), 2021 $7,110,000 refunding (0.20%-0.30%), and 2021 $33,315,000 refunding (0.30%-1.56%). Debt service to maturity totals $130,280,000 principal and $25,346,003 interest, or $155,626,003, with $17,809,407 due in 2022. The advance refunding paid $278,958 of issuance costs and used $1,425,000 of debt fund moneys, and the district reported seven debt service funds: 2012 Refunding, 2014, 2015 Refunding, 2016, 2019, 2021 Refunding Series A, and 2021 Refunding Series B.

**MPSERS.** Pension contribution rates ranged 13.39%-19.78% and OPEB rates 7.57%-8.43% for October 1, 2020 through September 30, 2021. Required and actual pension contributions were $27,611,786 and OPEB contributions $6,980,805. The net pension liability of $308,094,061 and net OPEB liability of $48,088,931 were measured as of September 30, 2020 from a September 30, 2019 valuation; proportions were 0.90 percent for both. Pension expense was $47,852,726 and OPEB recovery $860,940. Discount rates were 6.00-6.80 percent (pension) and 6.95 percent (OPEB), with a year-one health care cost trend rate of 7.00 percent. Payables to the plans were $7,516,769 and $951,164. RSI shows statutorily required pension contributions of $27,148,826 on covered payroll of $79,444,904 (34.17 percent) and OPEB contributions of $6,611,206 (8.32 percent).

**Other notes and statistics.** Bank deposits of $41,756,072 were uninsured and uncollateralized; MILAF holdings were $1,219,400 and $18,258,271, rated AAAm by S&P, totaling $19,477,671. Restricted assets comprised unspent bond proceeds and interest $19,533,470, sinking fund taxes $3,111,811, and debt service taxes $13,745,917. Unearned revenue included student lunch accounts $198,128, tuition and fees $429,407, and categorical aid $2,440,743. Operating lease costs were $122,804 (Troy Career Center building) and $89,112 (copiers), with future minimum payments of $246,356. Tax abatements reduced property tax revenue by $114,000, with about $99,000 reimbursed by the State. Tax year 2020 taxable value was $4,233,432,812 at a total rate of 23.0826 mills (homestead 4.6750, non-homestead 18.0000, debt 4.1000, sinking fund 0.9826); the levy of $60,779,142 produced total collections of $60,806,414, or 100.04 percent. Somerset Collections was the largest taxpayer at $58,558,600. Net general bonded debt was $137,615,624, 3.25 percent of taxable value, $1,576 per capita on a population of 87,294; the legal debt margin schedule shows a 2021 limit of $635,014,922 and margin of $505,078,261, while MD&A cites a $613.8 million statutory limit. Full-time equivalent employees totaled 985. Operating indicators for 2021 report cost per pupil of $12,942, revenue per pupil of $13,455, 813 teaching staff, 11.00 percent of students qualifying for free or reduced meals, and an average teacher salary of $75,918. The district operated 71 buses. For 2021-2022 the district budgeted a foundation allowance of $9,478 per pupil based on the May Consensus Revenue Estimating Conference estimate of a $163 per pupil increase, and after year end the School Aid Act delivered an additional $171 per pupil compared with 2020-2021.
